correctness.rationale: For k>=3 the local binary completion matrix has eigenvalues B=2^(k-1)-1 and -1. All-mixed counts are tr(M^r), while fixing at least one definite edge breaks the cycle into runs whose endpoint-conditioned counts multiply as entries of M^ell. The inequality m_a*m_b<=m_(a+b) with m_ell=(B^ell+1)/2 gives strict dominance over every profile with two or more definite edges, including ell=0. The all-mixed fiber strictly exceeds the exactly 2r single-definite runner-ups. The three-state transition trace enumerates realizable outputs. Independent brute-force calculations compared all output statuses for 161600 vertex subsets on eleven finite cases; this is corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact inverse-fiber spectrum is a natural measure of information lost by a three-way hyperedge observation, not just an arbitrary graph count. The theorem classifies the unique worst observation and all 2r runners-up for every cycle length and hyperedge rank, gives exact min-entropy and a growing rank-dependent asymptotic gap, and makes clear that the same observation count can conceal vastly different ambiguity. The known cyclic-word count is credited; value rests on the new extremal fiber structure and rank-2 boundary.
